neighbours.label: A slot inside a stock catchphrase formula (poor man's X, A Tale of Two X, rent-a-X, minimum viable X, the ultimate X, death by X)
fire: Critics called the sequel a poor man's Blade Runner.
The magazine ran a feature titled A Tale of Two Mayors.
He rented a van from a rent-a-wreck lot near the airport.
Investors asked the team to build a minimum viable prototype first.
Fans hail it as the ultimate guide to backyard grilling.
This cocktail is the thinking man's gin and tonic.
Staff complain about death by committee at the firm.
Think of quinoa as the poor man's caviar for dinner parties.
quiet: Critics called the sequel a slow remake of an old thriller.
The magazine ran a feature about two mayors in Ohio.
He rented a van from a small lot near the airport.
Investors asked the team to build a cheap prototype first.
Fans describe it as a useful guide to backyard grilling.
This cocktail is a mix of gin, tonic and lime.
Staff complain about long meetings at the firm.
Think of quinoa as a grain to serve at dinner parties.

notes: The pattern is a fixed formula waiting for its filler. Literal 'died by drowning' and 'two brothers' stayed quiet in probing; literal 'the poor man's hat' still fired, so the label is partly lexical.
